# Parley v0.1.30

This release changes how host vendor CLIs are launched. They now run with their
own permissions and approval prompts instead of inside Parley's outer Seatbelt
wrapper, so a vendor's own tool sandbox can start. Container panes keep their
existing reviewed boundary.

## Host vendor permissions

- Parley no longer wraps host vendor CLIs in its Seatbelt profile. That wrapper
  prevented Codex from applying its own tool sandbox, because macOS does not
  support the nested sandbox it needed.
- `AgentProcessBoundary` now applies only to a container pane's host Docker
  client. Docker continues to own the vendor's container boundary and reviewed
  mounts.
- Codex receives a native permission profile that denies Parley's private
  runtimes while allowing exact protocol and shim reads and writes to its own
  pane endpoint. Its built-in profile parent keeps Codex's Git and configuration
  protections. Those rules cover sandboxed tools, not the CLI parent,
  integrations or approved unsandboxed commands.
- Start, restart, resume and host team approval run a bounded preflight: a
  transient `codex app-server --stdio` reads configuration only, then
  `codex sandbox -P` exercises a real tool, synthetic private-file denials and
  own-endpoint access. Conflicting legacy sandbox settings are refused. This
  verifies configuration at that moment, not a future session's behaviour, and
  running processes are never silently restarted.
- Host bypass flags remain forbidden. Other vendors keep their existing native
  launch controls.

## What this means for isolation

- An unrestricted same-user host process can read another pane's credential or
  alter local records. Attribution is not isolation against such a process.
- Pane capabilities still authenticate and route explicit messages, and a valid
  token is still rejected through a different endpoint.
- Reviewed containers provide stronger separation, subject to their mounts and
  the trusted local Docker daemon. Human Shell panes remain unsandboxed.
- Native control now uses a fresh memory-only token, a natively supplied socket
  path and kernel peer-PID checks on both sides. The old control-token file is
  never read.

## Agent command runs

**Settings > General > Agent command runs** now holds two session choices rather
than durable ones. Automatic approval and closing clean run panes both start off
on every app launch and reset on quit. Neither preference domains, agent requests
nor the retired `command-run-authorization.json` can restore that authority. If
you use automatic approval for unattended work, expect to turn it back on after
each launch.

Approved worker tickets now carry a digest whose expected value stays in app
memory and travels as a literal launch argument, checked before the bytes are
decoded or executed. Editing the staged file cannot change the approved argv.
Result authentication does not protect against an unrestricted same-user process
reading a staged ticket's result key; treat captures as reported evidence.

## Core hardening

- Awaiting-review context Asks are now interrupted when Parley stops, instead of
  leaving the caller blocked until the 30-minute consultation timeout.
- `O_CLOEXEC` added to the relay credential lock and the inbox watcher, so a
  spawned child cannot inherit a lock descriptor and hold it.
- The control socket closes an accepted descriptor if the server is gone, and
  retries `recv` on `EINTR`.
- PTY mirroring retries briefly on a full buffer instead of dropping output, and
  interrupting a reviewed command run with Ctrl+C now returns the pane to an
  ordinary shell rather than ending its process.
- Context pack subprocesses no longer wait forever on a timed-out command whose
  grandchild holds the pipe open.

## Compatibility and validation

Agent protocol is now 32. Existing agent panes need a person-authorized restart
to receive the changed launch instructions; Parley never restarts them silently.

Validated on this branch: build, 326 native checks, 41 Node tests, public scan,
staged-secret scan, a 5/5 repeated control-socket regression and the 25-round
eight-pane Ghostty soak. A real installed Codex probe covered sandbox startup,
patching, private-path denials, own-endpoint access, read-only and inherited
`.git` protection, and legacy-config refusal. Details are in
`docs/host-permission-validation.md`.

Not yet exercised: fresh and resumed interactive vendor sessions, ordinary
permission prompts and protocol instruction uptake in an installed build. Treat
this beta as the first opportunity to check those.

Unnotarized test beta: ad-hoc signed without the hardened runtime, not
notarized, no automatic updates. Install only from the expected GitLab
release after checking SHA256SUMS.
